analysis.title: End of Week Market Intelligence: disruption interruption eruption
key_insights: US stocks were trading lower on Friday 20 Nov and on pace for a loss of more than 6% on the week for the S&P 500, as of 11:15AM Friday.

The selloff covers both sides of the AI trade. The SOX is down 7% on the week (infrastructure), and enterprise software names NOW, ORCL, CRM and SAP are down 10-15%+ on the week (AI disintermediation).
Risk-off sentiment is tied to doubts about earnings sustainability after four years of strong S&P 500 earnings growth, per Ben Snider's '2027 US Equity Outlook: The beginning of the middle.'
Amanda Lynam characterizes the credit environment as a 'three speed' market, more vulnerable to broad-based disruption, in '2027 Global Credit Outlook: Fading Tailwinds and a Growing AI Divide.'

Snider forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth falling 1200bp to 18% in 2027 from 30% this year. The note says investors may also be worried about downward EPS revisions replacing the sharp upward revisions of recent years.
Slower growth, downward revisions, and stubbornly high rates and oil prices are described as ingredients for a more subdued market. GS still forecasts a year-end 2027 S&P 500 target of 8700.

Snider focuses on 4 trades for a market moving away from AI infrastructure and from AI-disintermediated business models. These include defensives (Consumer Staples and the Midcap 400) and hyperscalers, which should see cash flow rise sharply if capex comes down.

Snider identifies 38 HALO stocks, physically intensive businesses that have cited AI productivity gains on earnings calls. The median stock in the group is down about 3% this week, well ahead of the S&P 500, and up about 17% YTD.

Next week is shortened for Thanksgiving, with a half-day on Friday. Data and events: October PCE inflation on Wednesday, Richmond Fed Index, Conference Board Consumer Confidence, home price data and the Fed Beige Book.
Next week's earnings include ADI, DELL, ADSK, HPE and WDAY on the tech side, and DE, A and J outside the AI trade.

sector_views.rationale: Snider includes Consumer Staples among 4 trades as a defensive for a market moving on from the AI infrastructure trade.
Hyperscaler cash flow should rise sharply if capex comes down.
Enterprise software names NOW, ORCL, CRM and SAP are down 10-15%+ on the week on AI disintermediation fears. The note gives no rating.

earnings_insights: Snider forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 18% in 2027, down 1200bp from 30% this year (GS forecast, not reported).
Consensus revisions for MSCI AC World EPS have been unusually positive (Exhibit 1). The note raises the possibility that revisions turn downward.
Upcoming earnings next week: ADI, DELL, ADSK, HPE, WDAY (tech) and DE, A, J (non-AI).

macro_indicators.interpretation: The note lists the print as a key data point for the shortened Thanksgiving week and gives no estimate.
GS expects a 1200bp slowdown in earnings growth.
GS keeps its year-end 2027 target despite the weekly selloff and slower growth.

trade_ideas.description: Buy HALO stocks, a basket of 38 physically intensive companies that cite AI productivity gains.
trade_ideas.rationale: The group has outperformed YTD with a median gain of about 17% and fell only about 3% this week.
